[MUQATIL:86:1-7/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The gushing water is the fluids of the man and woman, which adhere to one another and form the human.
[FARRA:v3p254#2/r9] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | Hijazi usage readily gives an active form a passive sense when it functions adjectivally, as in سر كاتم, وهم ناصب, ليل نائم, and عيشة راضية; the verse endings also favor it.
[MUSNAD-AHMAD:10399/r1] MUSNAD-AHMAD, d. 241 · رسول الله | reports | Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said everything was created from water, then prescribed greeting people, kind speech, keeping kin ties and night prayer as deeds leading to peaceful entry into Paradise.
[MUSNAD-AHMAD:7932/r1] MUSNAD-AHMAD, d. 241 · رسول الله | reports | Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said everything was created from water, then prescribed greeting people, feeding them, keeping kin ties and night prayer as deeds leading to peaceful entry into Paradise.

[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Dāfiq means madfūq, 'ejected'; it is an active form with passive sense.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Arabic also calls a night sleeping and a secret concealing, using an active participle for the object's state or effect.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · وعلة الجرمي | reports | Waʿila al-Jurmi's line calls the day aḥmas fājir, glossed as a hard day in which force is used.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r9] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | The author begins to note that faʿīl can mean mufʿil, but this excerpt supplies no example.
[TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | He challenges resurrection deniers to inspect their creation from emitted, poured fluid; two unnamed poetic lines use tarāʾib with gold, saffron, neck, and chest imagery as linguistic evidence.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | He glosses dāfiq as coming from above.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · سيبويه وأصحابه | reports | Sibawayh and his associates derive dāfiq by relation to effusion: it means water possessing an effusion.
[NAHHAS:v5p197/r11] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | مِمَّ contracts from مما; the alif is deleted because ما is interrogative, and the question is complete.
[NAHHAS:v5p197/r12] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الكسائي والفراء | reports | Al-Kisai and al-Farra take دافق to mean مدفوق, a passive sense expressed with an active participle.
[NAHHAS:v5p197/r13] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | rejects | Al-Nahhas rejects the active-for-passive explanation as false and non-analogical: if valid, ضارب could mean مضروب.
[NAHHAS:v5p197/r14] NAHHAS, d. 338 · البصريون | prefers | The Basrans analyze دافق as a relational adjective, as in an un-attributed poem’s ناصب and another’s نبال; both lines illustrate the adjective pattern.
[KHATTABI:v1p69/r1] KHATTABI, d. 388 · author | rejects | The imitator wrongly uses “faʿala” for the favor of pregnancy, since the expression typically evokes punishment; wording such as “showed kindness” or “bestowed favor” fits the intended meaning. | mentions 105:1, 4:147, 14:45
[THALABI:v10p179/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | “Dāfiq” is semen, poured into the womb; the active form carries a passive sense, as in “a concealed secret” and “a sleeping night.”
[THALABI:v10p179/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says the active-form usage is supported by the word’s position at the ends of the surrounding verses.
[THALABI:v10p179/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | “Dafq” means pouring; Arabs say a wave “tadaffaqa” or “indaffaqa” when it rises and falls.
[THALABI:v10p179/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The singular “water” means the two fluids of man and woman, from which the child is made, named one water because they mingle.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The gushing fluid comes from the father's loins and the mother's nurturing.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Reflection on human origin urges inference to God's complete power, knowledge, and will.
[JISHUMI:v10p7367/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The verse indicates that seminal-fluid components contribute to the child, even though other components join them before the child becomes alive.
[JISHUMI:v10p7367/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قيل | reports | Scholars disagree whether the child is created from the two fluids or from the man’s fluid alone.
[JISHUMI:v10p7367/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Remembering one’s humble origin and eventual fate after death should prevent arrogance.
[JISHUMI:v1p689/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The signs in creation include water apportioned to needs and made into rivers and springs; food for every animal; desire sustaining life; and God’s unique power to give life.
[JISHUMI:v1p689/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Further signs are varied forms and organs composed from flowing water, and life’s ordered stages from milk and food to speech, sensation, and reason.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The dāfiq water is semen poured into the womb; dāfiq means poured, though its active form carries a passive sense, as in “a pleasing life,” meaning one made pleasing (69:21). | mentions 69:21
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The singular water refers to both male and female fluids, since the child is formed from both and they mix together.

[TABRISI:86:1-17/r15] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Dafq is a forceful, abundant pouring; the reproductive fluid is called dāfiq for flowing and pouring out.
[TABRISI:86:1-17/r16] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Another grammatical explanation takes ماء دافق to mean مدفوق, like a concealed secret or a pleasing life.

[TABRISI:86:2-9/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | The human is created from semen, poured into the woman’s womb and from which the child develops.

[RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Dafq means pouring: the water is poured or flowing, and the verb describes a single outpouring.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r13] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · صاحب القول الثاني | reports | He further argues that dāfiq describes the man's fluid, and the following clause says this fluid exits from between loins and chest bones, supporting a male-only source.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r16] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · النبي | reports | A Prophetic report says the dominant man's fluid determines a boy and resemblance to his family, while the dominant woman's fluid determines resemblance to hers.

[RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A further explanation is metaphor: the fluid's owner is called flowing because he is the one who emits it.

[ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Though modern embryology is commonly pursued for medicine rather than theology, studying human formation can infer the Creator's power and clarify moral, religious, and human duties, so Elmalılı proceeds under the command to reflect.
